references.text: The parallel version of the tenth commandment in Exodus, which forbids coveting your neighbor's house, wife, male servant, female servant, ox, donkey, or anything else that belongs to your neighbor.
Proverbs warns against desire and greed, which lead to the destruction of one's own household.
The prophet Micah condemns those who covet fields and houses and seize them by force, a direct violation of the commandment against coveting.
Paul quotes the commandment 'You shall not covet' and explains how the law revealed sin in him.
Paul summarizes the commandments, including 'You shall not covet,' as being fulfilled by loving your neighbor as yourself.
Paul urges believers to avoid sexual immorality and all kinds of greed, which are linked to desire.
Paul identifies greed as idolatry and urges believers to put to death earthly desires, including coveting.
The exhortation to live without love for money and to be content with what one has is a practical application of the commandment against coveting.
James describes how desire leads to conflict and strife when people want what they do not have.
